definition: EN: A style of journalism in which journalists adopt a confrontational approach of reporting and interviewing—often within investigative or watchdog reporting—to scrutinize and challenge claims, expose inconsistencies, and hold powerful individuals or institutions accountable in service of the public.
(阐明观点或原因的)偏袒性(或倾向性)新闻报道;鼓吹性新闻;提倡某一事业(或表明某一观点)的报刊

EN: A type of journalism which deliberately adopts a non-objective viewpoint, usually committed to the endorsement of a particular social or political cause, policy, campaign, organization, demographic, or individual.
另类新闻学

EN: A type of journalism practiced in alternative media, typically by open, participatory, non-professionalized, non-commercial, and non-hierarchical media organizations. Precisely what is labeled alternative journalism has changed over time, but implicit in the genre is a rejection and critique of the practices of mainstream journalism, such that alternative journalists may perceive themselves as working to different values and ethics, covering different stories, giving access to a different cast of presenters and sources, or operating as a form of watchdog on mainstream media.
EN: A branch of journalism concerned with the reporting and discussion of the arts, including but not limited to the visual arts, film, literature, music, theater, and architecture.
n. 分配, 功课, 任务, 转让, 归因, 陈述
[计] 赋值
EN: An instruction to a reporter to cover an event.
EN: The bottom section of a story in a periodical, written ahead of the event it describes in order to save time in processing and completing the story before the publication deadline.
n. 政府官员举行的记者招待会
EN: A piece of journalism that accompanies or follows a news item and provides the audience with additional historical or other contextualizing information or analysis.
EN: Another name for the caption of a photograph.
a. 明亮的, 聪明的, 鲜明的, 欢快的
adv. 明亮地, 欢快地
EN: A short, amusing story.
n. 广播
[电] 广播

EN: The distribution of audio and audiovisual content to widely dispersed audiences through an electronic mass communications medium, traditionally via technologies that transmit radio waves to numerous recipients in a one-to-many model (as opposed to one-to-one transmission intended for a single recipient). The term generally includes distribution by radio, television, and Internet but excludes non-electronic forms of communication, even if they also reach a widespread audience, such as printed newspaper delivery.
[网络] 抄袭新闻;新闻抄袭

EN: A type of journalism that relies on recycling press releases and agency copy to fill newspaper pages or news bulletins, and which involves little or no independent reporting or attempt at verification.
EN: The use of a fictitious name for a byline, giving the impression that an article has been written by a member of the publication's staff when in fact it has been supplied by a news agency.
n. 专栏, 圆柱, 纵队, 列, 柱形物
[计] 列, 柱形图
EN: 1. A vertical block of text on a page, separated by margins and/or rules. Newspapers are commonly divided into visible columns.
n. 副本, 摹仿, 一册
v. 复印, 抄袭, 复制
[计] 副本; 复制; DOS内部命令:复制文件
将几个文件合并成一个文件, 以及将文件传至外设或在设备之间传送
EN: Written material intended for publication, as opposed to photographs or other elements of a publication's layout.
n. 通讯记者, 通信者
[经] 客户, 代理商行, 代理银行
EN: 1. A reporter who sends news to a newspaper office or broadcast headquarters remotely, i.e. from outside the office or headquarters.
EN: Reporting that ignores or treats lightly negative news about the friends of a particular reporter.
n. 正戏前的配戏,开场戏(开幕之前的短剧)
EN: A story written before a predicted event, setting the scene for when it happens. Such stories are often used at the start of election campaigns, sporting competitions, etc.
n. (插图下的)简短说明, 图片说明
EN: See caption.
a. 每日的, 日常的
adv. 每日地, 日常地
n. 日报
EN: A periodical for which new editions are published once per day, usually either on five days a week (every weekday), six days a week, or seven days a week (everyday including weekends).
n. 日期

EN: A line preceding a written news story that lists the name of the city, town, or general location from which the story is reported and sometimes the date, particularly for stories that are not considered local for the publication, i.e. reported from a distant location.
[机] 静气
EN: An extended unwanted silence that interrupts a radio or television broadcast, during which no audio or video program material is transmitted, usually caused by technical or operating errors.
n. 最后期限, 截止期限
[经] 截止日期
EN: The time set by the editor or producer by which a reporter must submit a finished story; the cut-off point for the completion of a story before it is published.
n. 甲板, (汽车后部的)行李仓
vt. 装饰, 打扮, 装甲板
[计] 纸牌背面图案
EN: 1. An individual row or line of type in a headline, e.g. a three-deck headline is set in three lines of text.
n. 数码鸿沟
[网络] 数字鸿沟;数位落差;数位差距

EN: Inequality between human populations in access to or effective use of digital technology, including online journalism and other forms of Internet-based or mobile communication, especially that due to social, economic, political, or cultural factors which may make one group more or less likely to make use of online content than other groups.

EN: The journalistic use of online social media to obtain the kind of information that in earlier eras would have required direct personal contact with the source, either face-to-face or on the telephone. The practice may include passive lifting of information, comments, or pictures from public social media profiles as well as direct requests for information or comments via social media.
编辑独立

EN: A concept in journalistic ethics holding that journalists ought to be able to conduct their work without coming under undue influence to provide coverage tailored to suit the commercial interests of proprietors or advertisers.
v. 发表社论, 插入主观评论
EN: To write in an opinionated and subjective manner, as in an editorial.
n. 尾注
[计] 尾注

EN: A paragraph presented after the end of an article, usually in a different type, giving additional information about the writer of the article, or, in the case of a review, the details of the publication or performance being reviewed.
a. 排外的, 独占的, 唯一的
[计] 独占的
EN: A story that a reporter or publication has obtained to the exclusion of the competition; a story to which only the reporting publication has access.

EN: A type of reporting that attempts to present ongoing news stories in a more accessible manner than conventional news sources by providing greater context and more detailed background information than might otherwise normally be provided in a traditional piece of journalism, with the goal of making the information understandable by a wider audience, including consumers who may not already be familiar with stylistic standards or industry-specific jargon associated with reporting on complex topics such as politics and law.
EN: A piece of investigative journalism that uncovers and makes public some form of allegedly scandalous behavior.
[网络] 证据核实;事实核对;事实核查

EN: The process of verifying the factual accuracy or otherwise establishing the veracity of the information reported within a piece of journalism, whether before or after the content is published or broadcast. Internal fact-checking may be done in-house by the publisher prior to publication (often by the original author or reporter, by an editor, and/or by persons employed specifically as fact-checkers) in order to prevent inaccurate content from being published, but external fact-checking is also commonly done by third parties after publication in an effort to promote accurate and reliably sourced reporting and call attention to any inaccuracies, misquotes, and other distortions of the truth.
n. 真实性,确凿性
EN: The factual quality of a piece of journalism.
n. 面孔的一部分(如眼、口等), 特征, 容貌, 特色, 特写
vt. 是...的特色, 特写, 放映
vi. 起重要作用
[计] 特性

EN: A story emphasizing the human or entertaining aspects of the situation it covers; a news story or other material that is highlighted as a special-interest piece or otherwise differentiated from straight news.

EN: A column or box printed in a regular, fixed position in each edition of a publication that lists the names and/or responsibilities of the publication's owners, departments, officers and staff, and/or contributors, as well as the physical addresses of the publication's offices and information on how to contact them.
<正>新闻界, 报界

EN: The press and the news media conceptualized as a distinctive estate of the realm, alongside the original three estates (nobility, commoners, and clergy) included in the traditional social hierarchy of much of Christian Europe. The notion refers particularly to the capacity of the media to wield great influence in politics and culture, and in some conceptualizations views them as quasi-constitutional watchdogs acting on behalf of a society's citizens. Compare fifth estate.
EN: To collect details for a story.
<德>n.(德国、奥地利、瑞典的) 伯爵
EN: An abbreviation for paragraph.
n. 排水沟, 槽, 贫民区
vt. 开沟于
vi. 流
[计] 装订线
EN: A vertical margin of white space where two pages meet, such as in the crease of a book or newspaper.
[计] 硬拷贝; 复印文本
[经] 复制件, 硬拷贝, 印刷记录
EN: Copy that is printed on physical paper, as opposed to soft copy, which exists in digital form.
n. 保镖( heavy的复数形式 ); 打手; 烈性啤酒; (尤指)苦啤酒
EN: An informal collective term for the broadcast or quality press, referring both to the physical weight of traditional printed newspapers and to their serious hard news content.
n. 毂, 木片, 中心
[计] 插座; 插孔; 集线器, 集中器, 连接器, 中继站

EN: A way of combining and/or centralizing editorial functions designed to break down traditional demarcations within a news organization, permitting many editors of distinct journalistic departments to work more closely together than they would by running their own separate divisions.
[美国英语]能唤起读者共鸣(或同情)的报道,“人情味”的故事

EN: A news story or feature, or an angle on a story, that tends to emphasize the emotion, drama, tension, struggle, joy, despair, triumph, or tragedy of people's lives, usually by focusing on individual people and the effects that specific issues or events have on them, or by covering unusual and interesting aspects of people's lives which are not particularly significant to society as a whole. Human-interest stories are not restricted to soft news, and in fact are often used to interest an audience in hard news by exploring individual case studies as a means of illustrating wider trends or statistics.
n. 直接, 目前, 迫切需要的事物

EN: The quality of an event or story that enables it to be reported as it is happening, or immediately after. All other things being equal, an unfolding or recent event is more likely than an older one to become news.
n. 插入物
vt. 插入, 把(人造卫星)射入(轨道), 添写
vi. 附着
[计] 插入
EN: 1. Additional text inserted into a story after it has been written, usually to provide additional details.
n. 新闻业, 报章杂志
[法] 报刊, 新闻业, 新闻出版

EN: The production and distribution of reports on current events based on facts and supported with proof or evidence, and practiced by professional or amateur journalists. Common types of journalistic media include print, television, radio, and the Internet.
跳页

EN: A line of type at the bottom of an incomplete newspaper or magazine article which directs the reader to another page where the story is continued. The term may also refer to the line at the top of the continued article indicating the page from which it was continued, also called a from line. See also spill.
n. 字距调整
[计] 字距调整
EN: A way of setting printed type so that the space between immediately adjacent characters is adjusted to appear uniform, at the same time reducing the amount of horizontal space they require.
n. 踢者, 善踢的人, 爱踢的马
[化] 抖动器
EN: 1. An entertaining, amusing, or offbeat story used to balance a page or bulletin of otherwise serious news.
n. 领导者, 社论, 指挥, 领袖, 领唱者, 前导字符
[计] 前导字符
EN: See editorial.
[法] 暗示性的讯问, 诱导证人回答的讯问
EN: A question phrased in such a way as to draw out a specific answer desired by the questioner.
[地名] [比利时] 莱德
EN: See lead.
(narrowcast 的现在分词) v.( 为少量特定听众)小范围播送,用电缆电视播送

EN: The dissemination of information to a specialized, niche, or narrowly defined target audience, rather than to a general one such as the public-at-large, in contrast to broadcasting. Target audiences may be defined by their shared demographic or common interests, or by being subscribers to a paid service.
通讯社

EN: A commercial organization that sells stories, photographs, or other journalistic products to the news media and which carries out reporting tasks on behalf of media clients. The Associated Press is an example.
[网络] 新闻周期;新闻循环

EN: The period of time that elapses before one news story or set of stories is replaced by another. Historically, news cycles have often been based on the publication deadlines of daily newspapers, typically lasting 24 hours, but for much of the public has continually decreased in duration with the emergence of radio, television, the Internet, and social media, such that cycles of definitive length have largely been supplanted by rolling news.
na. 〈美〉新闻窗口
[网络] 新闻版面;新闻洞;版面限制
EN: The amount of space available daily for news in a newspaper, after accounting for the space used by advertisements, attributions, images, etc.
[网络] 泄漏;消息来源

EN: The deliberate, surreptitious, and unauthorized release of confidential information to news media. It also refers to the premature publication of information by a news outlet that has agreed to delay release under a news embargo. News leaks can occur from sources or through breaches of agreed-upon timing, potentially affecting public perception and accountability.

EN: The qualities or criteria that journalists consider when assessing whether a story, event, development, or opinion is worthy of preparing and presenting as news. The process of determining what constitutes news may be complex and involve the weighing of a wide range of factors, including public interest, timeliness of the topic, reliability of the source, and the number of resources required to cover the story.
n. 新闻广播
EN: A news bulletin broadcast on radio or television, or a broadcast-style bulletin that can be viewed and/or listened to online.
n. 新闻广播员, 新闻评论广播员
EN: See news presenter.
n. 新闻纸
[化] 新闻纸

EN: A non-archival grade of paper on which newspapers and other publications and advertising material are commonly printed, consisting mainly of wood pulp and usually having an off-white cast and a soft, distinctive texture. It is favored by many daily broadsheets and wide-circulation publications because it is relatively lightweight, inexpensive, and durable and can accept simple four-color printing. It is often designed to be used in high-speed printing presses that print upon a continuous stream of paper rather than individual sheets.
a. 有报导价值的

EN: Describing the extent to which some event, statement, observation, story, or other piece of information has the potential to become news; the condition of being sufficiently notable or relevant to be covered or presented by the news media. Notions of what is newsworthy can differ markedly between mainstream and alternative journalism, with much of the latter's emphasis often predicated on an explicit rejection of conventional news values.
非正式地, 不可引用地
[法] 不公开的, 非正式的

EN: Information given by a source to a journalist on the (often implicit) understanding that, when reporting the information, the journalist will not attribute it to the source in a way that could allow readers to specifically identify the source. Contrast on the record.

EN: A story or publishable piece of information discovered through a journalist's own observation, investigation, initiative, or communication with contacts, as opposed to diary stories, which are generally predictable, publicly accessible events. Off-diary stories tend to be highly prized as they help to distinguish one news organization or brand from another.
记录在案的,公开发布的,公开做的

EN: Information given by a source to a journalist on the understanding that the journalist can publish it and openly and specifically attribute it to the source, as opposed to information shared "off the record", i.e. with the expectation that it will remain confidential and unattributed.
网路新闻学
EN: See digital journalism.
a. (报纸)专栏(版)的, 署名评论(版面)的

EN: A short opinion piece in written prose, typically less than 1,000 words, that expresses a strong, focused personal or collective opinion on an issue of relevance to the target audience, commonly included as a regular feature or column in many newspapers, magazines, and online publications. Op-eds are distinct from editorials and leaders, which are written by the publication's own staff, and often provide a space for commentary from outside contributors.

EN: A type of journalism that promotes interaction and two-way conversations between the journalist and his or her audience, often accompanied especially by the idea that access to online journalism should not be restricted by paywalls.
EN: A type of journalism that shares the journalist's commentary, analysis or opinion.
n. 前一天晚上, 一夜的逗留
a. 通宵的, 晚上的, 前夜的
adv. 在前一夜, 整夜, 昨晚一晚上
EN: A story written late at night in order to be published in the afternoon newspapers of the following day.
(许多记者)一窝蜂(或蜂拥而上)的新闻报道

EN: A practice in which multiple journalists representing different news organizations, even rival ones, act or work together with a sort of "pack mentality", reinforcing each other's views, approach, and/or actions while trying to provide coverage of the same story or event.

EN: The sudden emergence of national or international news organizations descending upon a location in order to cover a story rather than maintaining a permanent presence there or engaging local journalists to provide reporting. The term is often used to imply tactless efforts to obtain a desirable news story, in the absence of contextualizing information, respect for locals, or a true understanding of the issues involved.
n. 压, 揿, 按, 人群, 印刷机, 压力, 出版社, 记者, 报刊, 新闻舆论, 紧迫
vt. 压, 压榨, 紧抱, 逼迫, 推进, 强迫征募, 催逼
vi. 压, 重压, 催促, 拥挤, 奋力前进, 受压

EN: All forms of mass media considered collectively, especially print media such as newspapers and magazines but not necessarily excluding broadcast and online media; the journalism industry as a whole, or the entire body of journalists that produce and publish such media.
公共新闻学;公众新闻学

EN: Another name for civic journalism or citizen journalism; or any form of journalism that seeks to promote the participation and engagement of citizens in democratic governments and civic structures, and/or to bemoan the absence of active involvement of the general public in conventional journalism and commercial mass media.

EN: Any form of journalism that articulates a critical perspective on society or eschews the established conventions of mainstream journalism, often found in alternative media and the underground press; the collective body of publications endorsing this style of journalism is sometimes referred to as the radical press.
n. 暗色毛边引文

EN: The reproduction of a section of a previously reported story, usually comprising the headline and intro, as a "cut-out" graphic alongside a follow-up story, in order to remind readers of the earlier coverage. A rag-out is often outlined with a jagged border to give the impression of it having been torn from the original page.
n. 伸出, 延伸, 区域, 范围, 流域, 岬
vt. 到达, 达到, 伸出, 延伸, 影响
vi. 达到, 延伸, 伸出手, 传到
EN: A measure of the potential size of an audience for a particular publication, program, or website, as opposed to a measure of the actual number of people reading, watching, or listening to it.
n. 右页, (纸的)正面
EN: The right-hand page of a newspaper or periodical. Contrast verso.
n. 缩进, 撤回
[医] 退缩, 缩回
EN: A published correction (especially in print) that formally withdraws a false or offending piece of journalism and/or acknowledges that it was incorrectly or misleadingly reported.
n. 路透社
EN: An international news agency founded in London in 1851 that provides news material in 16 languages and numerous multimedia formats to subscribing news media organizations worldwide.
[网络] 滚动新闻;滚动消息
EN: News that is broadcast on a continuous basis rather than being confined to specific bulletins.
EN: A story that attempts to correct a previous story without indicating that the prior story had been in error or without taking responsibility for the error.
动作次序
EN: A list from first to last of which stories will feature in a broadcast news bulletin. Changes are sometimes made at the last minute, or even after the broadcast has begun.
新闻保障法

EN: Any legislation designed to protect reporters' privilege by preventing a journalist from being compelled to reveal the identity of an anonymous source who has been promised confidentiality. The term is used primarily in the United States.
n. 衬衣下摆, 社论栏
a. 幼小的, 远房的
EN: A short, related story added to the end of a longer one.
n. 鼻涕虫, 刺蛾, 懒汉, 弹丸, 金属小块, 重击
vi. 偷懒, 动作迟缓
vt. 重击

EN: A working title given to a story as it proceeds through production but prior to final publication. Normally just one word, slugs are intended to be seen only by journalists and reporters in the office or studio.
[计] 软拷贝
EN: Copy that exists in digital form as computerized data, as opposed to hard copy, which is printed on a physical medium.
软新闻

EN: Any news that is not hard news, typically stories covering topics regarded as inconsequential or light-hearted, or which are reported more for their entertainment value and to balance somber and serious content than because of their importance to public knowledge.
[化] 掺加; 掺加示踪剂
EN: The act of withholding a story from publication, either temporarily or permanently, for editorial, political, or commercial reasons.
n. 旋转, 自旋, 疾驰, 情绪低落
vt. 纺织, 纺, 使旋转, 编造
vi. 纺纱, 吐丝, 作茧, 结网, 旋转, 自旋, 疾驰

EN: A particular angle or interpretation of information or events, especially one which deliberately ignores or contradicts other information which might undermine its own validity or otherwise fails to adhere to standards of objectivity; or the practice of pushing such a biased angle with the goal of influencing journalistic coverage and ultimately public opinion. Spin is thus a form of propaganda and generally has a negative connotation which implies willful distortion of the truth through the use of disingenuous, deceptive, or manipulative tactics. The term is most commonly applied to press officers working for politicians, though it may also be used more broadly to describe any effort to man
n. 飞溅, 污点, 一点儿, 溅泼声, 色斑
vi. 溅湿, 溅开, 飞溅
vt. 溅, 泼, 使溅起水, 洒, 使成斑驳状
EN: An exciting or widely interesting front-page story given prominence so that people will take notice of the publication in which it is printed.
n. 特约撰稿人
EN: A person, often an intern, whom a publication such as a magazine employs to propose ideas for articles, write them and sometimes do clerical and research work.
vt. 为(报刊文章)写摘要或内容提要

EN: A sentence or two of text placed immediately beneath the headline but before the main body of an article, which serves to introduce or contextualize what follows. Standfirsts most commonly accompany feature stories and may also incorporate the writer's byline. See also go-last.
纯新闻;直述新闻
EN: See hard news.
n. 横幅, 饰带, 流光, 通栏标题
EN: See banner.
(streeter 的复数) [人名] [英格兰人姓氏] 斯特里特 Street的变体; [地名] [美国] 斯特里特
EN: See vox pop.
n. 纵梁, 楼梯基, 上弦工人, 出售弓弦的人, 制造弓弦的人
EN: A freelance journalist who contributes writing, photos, videos, or other content to a news or photo agency and is paid for each contribution rather than with a fixed salary.
n. 线, 丝, 纤维, 线索
vt. 穿线于, 穿过, 通过, 用线穿成
vi. 穿过
[计] 线索, 线程
EN: A series of Internet posts on a single topic.
n. <网球>上旋
EN: An intangible quality that journalists are sometimes said to apply to their stories in order to make them appear more relevant or significant than they actually are. See also spin.

EN: An international news agency founded in 1907 and based in the United States that offers newswires, photographs, film, and audio services in English, Spanish, and Arabic to subscribing news media organizations worldwide.
n. 偶数页, 背面, 反面
EN: The left-hand page of a newspaper or periodical. Contrast recto.
监督新闻学;看门狗新闻学

EN: A form of investigative journalism in which journalists, authors or publishers of a news publication fact-check and interview political and public figures to increase accountability in democratic governance systems.
n. 网路广播;网络广播;网络直播

EN: A media presentation distributed, either live or on demand, over the Internet using streaming media to distribute a single content source to many listeners or viewers simultaneously, i.e. "broadcasting" on the "web".

EN: White text on a black or dark-coloured background; an abbreviation of white on black.
黄色报刊
EN: American newspapers that engage in yellow journalism.

替代新闻群组

天体物理学新闻组

新闻背景
